## Description

{gtsummary} is the most widely used R package for creating
presentation-ready summary tables across the R ecosystem. Because it is
built for broad utility across multiple domains, its flexibility and
customization ability lends itself to the diverse needs in clinical
trial reporting.

In this workshop, we will begin with a brief overview of {gtsummary}
fundamentals before diving into the key tooling and strategies that make
enterprise adoption smooth and effective. Participants will learn:

-   **Analysis Results Data (ARD) Integration:** How {gtsummary} and
    ARDs work seamlessly together by design to support reproducible,
    clinical-grade workflows.

-   **Custom Themes for Standardization:** How to build company-specific
    themes that alter defaults, ensuring output automatically aligns
    with internal guidelines without requiring repetitive argument
    specifications.

-   **Building Custom Extensions:** When and how to supplement
    {gtsummary} with a supplemental R package to handle specialized
    reporting needs, leveraging {gtsummary}'s extension framework to
    simplify development.

By the end of the session, you will understand how to extend this
open-source tool with institution-specific functionality to balance
flexibility with company-wide standardization.

## Getting started

The workshop is hands-on. You can work through the exercises either in
**Posit Cloud** or **on your own machine** — whichever you prefer. Get
set up now; we'll walk through it together at the top of the session.

Bookmark this site either way. You'll reference it throughout the
workshop, and the exercise code lives on the
[Exercises + Solutions](exercises/exercises.qmd) page.

### Option 1: Posit Cloud

Nothing to install — the workshop packages are already there. R/Pharma
has granted everyone **$2 of AI credits** to use during the workshop.

**How to start your workshop assignment**

1.  **Join the space.** The link will be provided during the workshop.

2.  **Locate the project.** Find
    `rpharma-workshop-gtsummary-adoption-2026` under the **All Content**
    tab.

3.  **Create your copy.** Click on the project name, then click the
    **Save a Copy** banner at the top of the screen (or the **Start**
    button, if the project is set up as a template).

4.  **Begin working.** Posit Cloud duplicates the project into your
    personal workspace, creating your own independent version where you
    can write and save code.

### Option 2: Your own machine

Install the workshop packages — this takes a few minutes, so start it
before we get going. Open Positron/RStudio/your IDE alongside Zoom, and
run:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse",
                   "cards",
                   "cardx",
                   "gtsummary",
                   "broom.helpers",
                   "flextable",
                   "pharmaverseadam"))
```

This is the same as
[`install.R`](https://github.com/ddsjoberg/rpharma-workshop-gtsummary-adoption-2026/blob/main/install.R)
in the workshop repo.
